main_body: A low wooden feed trough: a green hay/grass fill heaped along the top (rows ~4-9), a pale cream rim line at row 9, an orange-brown upper board (rows 10-11), a dark gap, then a brown plank front with a notch/post pattern (rows 12-14).
top_band: Green hay/grass fill, rows ~4-9, lumpy and irregular, reads as contents seen from the front. There is a cream line at row 9 and an orange band at rows 10-11 below it. There is no distinct lighter horizontal top surface that reads as a rim around an opening.
evidence: The column through the middle runs: green hay (rows 4-8), cream line (row 9), orange band (rows 10-11), dark line (row 12), brown plank (rows 12-14). The hay is a bush-like mound seen from the front, not the inside of an opening seen from above. The trough has no back rim, no front rim and no ellipse that shows an interior. The wooden part is a flat front elevation made of horizontal bands, and the only top-like feature is a 1-2px cream line. The planks are painted flat with no inset. The object is also cropped at the bottom of the tile. The opening is not visible as an interior surface, so it fails the container requirement.

style.evidence: The hay has 4-5 greens with yellow flecks, which gives decent texture and is comparable to the reference's grass tuft. The wooden trough is thin, with 2-3 flat tones: the orange band and the brown planks are nearly flat fills with little grain, and there are no per-plank highlights or knots. The dark brown outline is tinted, which is good. The wood is weaker than the reference's richly shaded stall and well, so the piece sits below the reference overall.
